turns.content: My wedding is six weeks away. My closest friend Rohan is supposed to be in my haldi and give a toast — he's been my guy since first year of college. But every time I bring up his travel from Bangalore he just says "let's see, I'll definitely try." Should I just book his flight myself and be done with it?

Hey, that sounds really stressful with the wedding so close. Rohan being there for the haldi and the toast clearly means a lot to you, especially after all those years.

His “let’s see, I’ll definitely try” answers are pretty vague, though. It might be work, money, or something he’s not saying yet. Booking the flight yourself could feel like a generous push, but it also risks putting him on the spot or leaving you out of pocket if he still can’t make it.

I’d talk to him first, just the two of you. Tell him straight how much his presence matters and ask what’s actually going on. That conversation will tell you more than any ticket purchase. If after that he still wants to come but the logistics are the only hold-up, then offering to book it becomes a kind gesture instead of a surprise.

You’ve got this. Six weeks is tight, but you’ve handled bigger things with him before. What’s your gut saying about why he’s being so non-committal?

I checked, flights are like nine thousand return. Not crazy. He switched jobs a couple of months back, some startup. And lately his replies are two words where he used to send voice notes. I'm telling myself he's busy but it's been weeks of this.

Yeah, nine thousand isn’t nothing, but it’s not a fortune either — especially if you’ve already budgeted for the people who matter. The bigger thing is the shift you’re noticing: two-word replies instead of those long voice notes, and this dragging on for weeks. That’s the part that stings, not the ticket price.

A new startup job can swallow people whole — insane hours, constant firefighting, maybe even some money tightness while he figures out the first few paychecks. It doesn’t automatically mean he doesn’t care, but it also doesn’t excuse leaving you hanging when the wedding is six weeks out.

I’d still talk to him before you hit “book.” Something simple and direct: “Bro, I need a yes or no on the dates. The haldi and toast mean a lot and I don’t want to keep guessing. What’s actually going on?” Give him the chance to be honest — whether it’s work, cash, or something else. If after that conversation the only barrier is the flight, then offering to book it becomes a real gift instead of a gamble.

You’ve known him since first year; you can probably tell when he’s just buried versus when he’s pulling away. What’s your read on which one this feels like?

Honestly it's starting to hurt now. If he actually cared he would have just said yes on day one, no? I'm thinking I should just call him tonight and ask him straight — "bro, are you coming or not, yes or no." At least I'll know where I stand.

Yeah, that hurt is real. When someone who’s been your person since first year starts giving two-word answers and “let’s see” for something this big, it does start to feel like maybe the care isn’t matching what you thought it was. You’re allowed to feel that.

Calling him tonight and asking straight — “Bro, are you coming or not? I need a yes or no” — is actually the kindest thing you can do for both of you right now. No more guessing, no more hoping the next message will be different. You’ll know where you stand, and he won’t be able to keep floating.

Just go in ready for whatever answer comes. If it’s a yes, great, then you can talk flights. If it’s a no or another dodge, at least you’ll have the truth instead of this slow drip of maybe. You’ve got six weeks; better to know tonight than keep carrying it.

You’ve got this. Call him, say it clearly, and then take care of yourself after, whatever he says. I’m here if you want to talk after the call.

My fiancée says I'm overthinking and he's probably just swamped. But this is the same guy who took an overnight bus to be at my sister's wedding in 2019. Something has changed and I can't figure out what, and I hate that I'm angry at him two weeks before my haldi.

That contrast hits hard. The guy who jumped on an overnight bus for your sister’s wedding in 2019 is now giving you two-word replies and “let’s see” for *your* wedding. Of course that feels like something’s shifted, and of course you’re angry. You’re allowed to feel that, even if your fiancée thinks you’re overthinking it. Being swamped at a new startup can explain a lot, but it doesn’t erase the difference you’re seeing.

The anger two weeks out makes sense too — this is supposed to be one of the happiest stretches, and instead you’re carrying this uncertainty about someone who’s been your person since first year. That’s exhausting.

Calling him tonight and asking straight is still the cleanest move. You’ll either get the yes you need or the honesty that’s been missing. Either way, you’ll stop living in this limbo.

After the call, whatever he says, give yourself a minute. You’ve got a wedding coming and people who *are* showing up. What’s the first thing you want to say when you dial? I’m right here if you want to talk after.
